rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers imagine resurrection impossible once their bodies have been scattered through the earth.
rows.anchor: أي: تمزقت أجسامنا وتفرقت في أجزاء الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection reflects only their incapacity: the Creator who originated them from nothing can restore them by His command.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما هو بعيد بالنسبة إلى قدرتهم العاجزة، لا بالنسبة إلى قدرة الذي بدأهم وخلقهم من العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies their rejection as disbelief in meeting their Lord.
rows.anchor: بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's wording indicates that the Angel of Death is a specific angel assigned to take souls.
rows.anchor: الظاهر من هذه الآية أن ملك الموت شخص معين من الملائكة

rows.speaker: قتادة وغير واحد
rows.claim: Some reports, including Qatada's, call the Angel of Death Azrael, the commonly known name; he has assistants.
rows.anchor: وقد سمي في بعض الآثار بعزرائيل، وهو المشهور، قاله قتادة وغير واحد، وله أعوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the Angel of Death's assistants draw souls from the body, then the Angel of Death takes them when they reach the throat.
rows.anchor: ورد في الحديث أن أعوانه ينتزعون الأرواح من سائر الجسد، حتى إذا بلغت الحلقوم تناولها ملك الموت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, so he can take souls from wherever he wishes.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: حويت له الأرض فجعلت له مثل الطست

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad relays a similar account from the Prophet as a mursal report.
rows.anchor: ورواه زهير بن محمد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، بنحوه مرسلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also transmits the account that the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin.
rows.anchor: وقالَه ابن عباس، رضي الله عنهما.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Ja'far ibn Muhammad's father, the Prophet asks the Angel of Death to treat a believing companion gently; the angel says he is gentle to every believer, inspects every home five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito's soul without God's command.
rows.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يا ملك الموت، ارفق بصاحبي فإنه مؤمن". فقال ملك الموت: يا محمد، طب نفسا وقر عينا

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Ja'far says the Angel of Death inspects people at prayer times; when a person who kept prayer is dying, the angel approaches, repels Satan, and prompts the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر: بلغني أنه إنما يتصفحهم عند

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Angel of Death visits every house, whether tent or masonry, twice each day.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: حدثنا محمد بن مسلم، عن إبراهيم بن ميسرة قال: سمعت مجاهدا يقول

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the Angel of Death stands at the door of every inhabited house seven times daily, checking whether anyone there is due to die.
rows.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والله ما من بيت فيه أحد من أهل الدنيا إلا وملك الموت يقوم على بابه كل يوم سبع مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to the Lord means resurrection from the graves on the appointed day for recompense.
rows.anchor: يوم معادكم وقيامكم من قبوركم لجزائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands believers to remember Him abundantly because He has bestowed many kinds of blessings, bringing great reward and a good return.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى آمرا عباده المؤمنين بكثرة ذكرهم لربهم تعالى، المنعم عليهم بأنواع النعم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet teaching that remembrance of God is the best and purest deed, raises ranks, and surpasses charity in gold and silver or fighting an enemy.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi notes that some transmitters reported the Abu al-Darda hadith as mursal.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي: ورواه بعضهم عنه فأرسله

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes a similar report through Mu'adh ibn Jabal from the Prophet, and says God knows best.
rows.anchor: أنه بلغه عن معاذ بن جبل، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، بنحوه، فالله أعلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Huraira says he keeps a prayer he heard from the Prophet: asking God to make him most grateful, most attentive to counsel, most given to remembrance, and most protective of the divine charge.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: دعاء سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أدعه

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Abu Huraira supplication report gharīb.
rows.anchor: ورواه الترمذي عن يحيى بن موسى

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد المدني
rows.claim: Ahmad also transmits the same supplication from Abu Huraira through Abu Sa'id al-Madani.
rows.anchor: عن فرج بن فضالة، عن أبي سعيد المدني

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best person is one whose life is long and deeds good; when asked for a practice to hold fast to amid many Islamic duties, he says to keep the tongue moist with remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن بسر يقول: جاء أعرابيان إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should glorify God in the morning and evening, as in the verse naming the times people enter evening and morning and other parts of the day.
rows.anchor: أي: عند الصباح والمساء، كقوله: {فسبحان الله حين تمسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's and the angels' blessings on believers spur them to remember Him: since He remembers them, they should remember Him, as the cited command says.
rows.anchor: هذا تهييج إلى الذكر، أي: إنه سبحانه يذكركم فاذكروه أنتم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A divine hadith promises that whoever remembers God privately is remembered privately, and whoever remembers Him in a gathering is remembered in a better gathering.
rows.anchor: يقول الله: من ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي، ومن ذكرني في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير منهم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains God's salat as His praise of the servant before the angels; al-Bukhari relates the view through al-Rabi' ibn Anas.
rows.anchor: والصلاة من الله ثناؤه على العبد عند الملائكة، حكاه البخاري عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation takes God's salat to mean mercy, supported by the verse describing God's blessings and mercy upon the patient.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: الصلاة من الله: الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir sees no contradiction between God's praise of believers before the angels and His mercy toward them.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال: لا منافاة بين القولين والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' salat means supplication for people and asking forgiveness, as shown by the angels' prayer for believers.
rows.anchor: وأما الصلاة من الملائكة، فبمعنى الدعاء للناس والاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through His mercy, praise, and the angels' prayers, God brings believers from the darkness of ignorance and error into the light of guidance and certainty.
rows.anchor: بسبب رحمته بكم وثنائه عليكم، ودعاء ملائكته لكم، يخرجكم من ظلمات الجهل والضلال إلى نور الهدى واليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy in this life guides believers to truth and shows them the path from which others, including callers to disbelief or innovation and their followers, have strayed.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا: فإنه هداهم إلى الحق الذي جهله غيرهم، وبصرهم الطريق الذي ضل عنه وحاد عنه من سواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the afterlife, God protects believers from the greatest terror and sends angels to greet them with news of Paradise and rescue from Hell, out of love and compassion.
rows.anchor: وأما رحمته بهم في الآخرة: فآمنهم من الفزع الأكبر، وأمر ملائكته يتلقونهم بالبشارة بالفوز بالجنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that when a mother rushed to save her child, the Prophet said God would not cast His beloved into the Fire; Ibn Kathir says its chain meets the conditions of the two Sahih collections, though none of the six included it.
rows.anchor: فخفضهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال: "ولا الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir also cites Umar's report in al-Bukhari: God is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child.
rows.anchor: فوالله، لله أرحم بعباده من هذه بولدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the one, self-sufficient deity, with no equal or partner; He independently governs all things without rival or opponent.
rows.anchor: أنه الإله الواحد الأحد، الفرد الصمد، الذي لا نظير له ولا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings called upon besides God own not even an atom's weight in the heavens or earth, as another verse says they do not own a date-stone's skin.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السموات ولا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false gods neither own anything independently nor share ownership with God, and none of them supports Him in any affair.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون شيئا استقلالا ولا على سبيل الشركة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the denied helper as one who assists God with anything.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله: {وما له منهم من ظهير}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of God's greatness and majesty, no one may intercede with Him unless He first grants permission, as other verses also teach.
rows.anchor: لا يجترئ أحد أن يشفع عنده تعالى في شيء إلا بعد إذنه له في الشفاعة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the sound collections, the Prophet describes his supreme intercession: he prostrates, is taught praise, then is told to raise his head, ask, and intercede, and his request is granted.
rows.anchor: فأسجد لله فيدعني ما شاء الله أن يدعني، ويفتح علي بمحامد لا أحصيها الآن، ثم يقال: يا محمد، ارفع رأسك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومسروق وغيرهما
rows.claim: When God speaks revelation, the inhabitants of heaven hear Him and tremble with awe until they nearly swoon.
rows.anchor: إذا تكلم بالوحي، سمع أهل السموات كلامه، أرعدوا من الهيبة حتى يلحقهم مثل الغشي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والشعبي وإبراهيم النخعي والضحاك والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: These authorities explain fuzzi'a as fear being cleared away from their hearts; some early readers, in a reading also reported as Prophetic, read faraġa with ghayn, which returns to the same meaning.
rows.anchor: والضحاك والحسن، وقتادة في قوله تعالى: {حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم} يقول: جلى عن قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the fear passes, the bearers of the Throne tell the angels nearest them what God said, who pass it down in sequence until it reaches the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: فيخبر بذلك حملة العرش للذين يلونهم، ثم الذين يلونهم لمن تحتهم، حتى ينتهي الخبر إلى أهل السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels report God's words truthfully, without adding or omitting anything.
rows.anchor: أي: أخبروا بما قال من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the verse about polytheists at death or resurrection, when they awaken from worldly heedlessness, regain their reason, and hear that the truth was what God said.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى قوله: {حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم} يعني: المشركين عند الاحتضار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the covering is removed from the polytheists' hearts on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم}

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains the phrase as the removal of the doubt and denial in their hearts.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: {حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم} يعني: ما فيها من الشك والتكذيب

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Satan, his delusions, and the doubts in people's hearts depart; this concerns human beings at death, when they admit the truth too late for the admission to help them.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: {حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم} يعني: ما فيها من الشك، قال: فزع الشيطان عن قلوبهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the first interpretation, that the pronoun refers to the angels; Ibn Kathir calls this certainly correct because sound hadiths and reports support it.
rows.anchor: وقد اختار ابن جرير القول الأول: أن الضمير عائد على الملائكة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Huraira reports that when God decrees a matter in heaven, angels beat their wings in submission; after they recover from awe, they ask what God said and relay the truth. Jinn overhear fragments and pass them to soothsayers, who mix a true word with a hundred lies; Ibn Kathir says al-Bukhari alone gives this route, also cited by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah.
rows.anchor: يقول: أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا قضى الله الأمر في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Muslim’s four routes pass through al-Zuhri, Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Ibn Abbas from one Ansari man; Yunus says several Ansar, al-Nasa’i cites al-Zubaydi, and al-Tirmidhi’s route goes through Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري، عن علي بن الحسين، عن ابن عباس عن رجل من الأنصار، به

rows.speaker: النواس بن سمعان
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when God intends revelation, the heavens shake, angels faint and prostrate, Gabriel receives the message, and angels in each heaven ask what God said; Gabriel answers, 'the truth,' and carries it where God commands. Ibn Abi Hatim records the report; Ibn Kathir says Ibn Jarir and Ibn Khuzayma also transmit it, while Abu Hatim says it is not known in Syria from al-Walid ibn Muslim.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا أراد الله أن يوحي بأمره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada interpret the verse as referring to God's beginning revelation to Muhammad after the interval between him and Jesus.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس -وعن قتادة: أنهما فسرا هذه الآية بابتداء إيحاء الله سبحانه إلى محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the beginning of revelation to Muhammad is undoubtedly the clearest application included in this verse.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن هذا أولى ما دخل في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Judgment, God publicly rebukes polytheists who claimed to worship angel-shaped idols to bring them nearer to Him, asking the angels whether they commanded this worship.
rows.anchor: يسأل الملائكة الذين كان المشركون يزعمون أنهم يعبدون الأنداد التي هي على صورة الملائكة ليقربوهم إلى الله زلفى

rows.speaker: الملائكة
rows.claim: The angels glorify God and disavow the polytheists, affirming that they are God's servants and that the worshippers instead served the jinn.
rows.anchor: وهكذا تقول الملائكة: {سبحانك} أي: تعاليت وتقدست عن أن يكون معك إله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn here mean devils, who beautify idol worship for people and lead them astray; most polytheists believed in those devils.
rows.anchor: {بل كانوا يعبدون الجن} يعنون: الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day, the false gods cannot benefit or harm their worshippers, who had hoped their idols would help in times of distress; the polytheists are told to taste the Fire they denied.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يقع لكم نفع ممن كنتم ترجون نفعه اليوم من الأنداد والأوثان، التي ادخرتم عبادتها لشدائدكم وكربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has sealed the persistently disbelieving people in misguidance, so warning them brings no benefit and has no effect.
rows.anchor: قد ختم الله عليهم بالضلالة، فما يفيد فيهم الإنذار ولا يتأثرون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only believers who follow the Qur'an benefit from the warning; fearing the Merciful unseen means knowing that God sees and knows what they do even when no one else does.
rows.anchor: {إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر} أي: إنما ينتفع بإنذارك المؤمنون الذين يتبعون الذكر، وهو القرآن العظيم، {وخشي الرحمن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning brings such people forgiveness of their sins and a great, abundant, beautiful reward, like the reward promised to those who fear God unseen.
rows.anchor: {فبشره بمغفرة} أي: لذنوبه، {وأجر كريم} أي: كبير واسع حسن جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will raise the dead on Resurrection Day; the verse also hints that He can revive the dead hearts of some disbelievers by guiding them from error to truth.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى يحيي قلب من يشاء من الكفار الذين قد ماتت قلوبهم بالضلالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the greeting as God Himself being peace to the people of Paradise, paralleling the verse that says their greeting when meeting Him is peace.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال ابن عباس في قوله: {سلام قولا من رب رحيم} فإن الله نفسه سلام على أهل الجنة.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Lord appears to the people of Paradise, greets them with peace, and they gaze at Him, giving no attention to other bliss until He is veiled; Ibn Kathir says the report's chain is questionable, and Ibn Majah also transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "بينا أهل الجنة في نعيمهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Through Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Muhammad ibn Ka'b describes God greeting the people of Paradise after judgment; they ask for His pleasure, which He grants by settling them in the abode of honor, then gives them further gifts carried by angels.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان بن حميد قال: سمعت محمد بن كعب القرظي يحدث عن عمر بن عبد العزيز قال: إذا فرغ الله من أهل الجنة والنار
